author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: A read-only page in the vet feature package, built from patterns already in force (system-design.md § Contracts, architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog). The adjustments: (1) a SpecialtyRepository mirroring PetTypeRepository, the lookup-value repository precedent, because an unheld specialty (edge case 4) is not reachable through Vet; (2) a SpecialtyDirectory value object that inverts veterinarians into per-specialty holder lists and owns both orderings (edge case 5), keeping the Web controller row clean of any rule; (3) a separate SpecialtyController for the new HTTP surface, so VetController and its tests stay untouched (the prd-entry's VetController file target is best-effort; this placement supersedes it). The new Scale and Load section carries the page's row. Backing: grep on src/main/java/.../vet and owner/PetTypeRepository.java, the weaker basis since no IDE oracle is connected.
integration_points: SpecialtyRepository: Spring Data Repository<Specialty, Integer> exposing every stored specialty; no ordering in the query and no @Cacheable. SpecialtyDirectory does the sorting.

SpecialtyDirectory: an immutable record built by a static factory from the specialties and the veterinarians. It holds one listing per specialty in name order, each with its holders ordered by last name, then first name. Lists are defensive copies. Imports no Spring or JPA type.

SpecialtyController: GET /specialties.html, with no @RequestParam and no @ModelAttribute. It reads SpecialtyRepository and the cached VetRepository.findAll(), builds SpecialtyDirectory, adds it to the model, and returns vets/specialtyList. Collaborators arrive through the constructor (Design Principle 3).
Binding: the new entry point binds no request data, so it has no binding target. No persisted type is bound.

Template: vets/specialtyList.html uses the fragments/layout wrapper (standard navigation, REQ-SYS-001) and renders each holder as firstName + ' ' + lastName, as vetList.html does. An unheld specialty renders the existing #{none} key. Specialty names render as stored (th:text, escaped). Do not add a menuItem or any link to /specialties.html in layout.html or any other template.
Messages: every new key (page heading at minimum) goes into all eleven bundles plus the base messages.properties. I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces this (REQ-LANG-002).

Double, repository boundary (unit tests): none. SpecialtyDirectoryTests exercises the value object with real Vet and Specialty instances. It covers ACs 2-6: full name, unheld veterinarian absent, multi-specialty holder under each, unheld specialty listed with no holders, and both orderings.

Double, repository boundary (web tests): hand-written in-memory implementations of VetRepository and SpecialtyRepository, supplied to @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class) through an imported @TestConfiguration. No @MockitoBean (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy: hand-written first).

Double, framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned one. SpecialtyControllerTests covers the route, the view, single-page rendering with no pagination controls, the standard navigation, and the rendered held-by-none wording.

No-link criterion: a test that scans src/main/resources/templates for any reference to specialties.html outside specialtyList.html, walking the templates the way I18nPropertiesSyncTest does. It covers every existing page without rendering each one.

patterns.description: thin read-only controller shape; constructor-injected repository
full-name rendering and #{none} for the empty case
Value object row for SpecialtyDirectory; Web controller row bars the grouping and ordering from SpecialtyController

risks.risk: Specialty and Vet do not override equals. Specialties from SpecialtyRepository and those inside cached Vet instances are different object instances, so identity or Set membership silently matches nothing.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory matches holders by specialty id (BaseEntity identity). A unit test builds the specialty list and the vets' specialties as distinct instances that share ids (architecture-principles.md § Domain Core: invariants in the value object).

risks.risk: VetRepository.findAll() returns shared cached Vet instances (vets cache, Open Question 5).
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory only reads them and copies references into its own lists. It never mutates a Vet or a Specialty.

risks.risk: Specialty directory page scales with specialties times holders (system-design.md § Scale and Load, specialty directory row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one uncached all-specialties query plus the cached vet collection, grouped in memory. No pagination, per the requirement.

risks.risk: Specialty names are stored data echoed into HTML (security-principles.md, cross-site scripting row).
risks.mitigation: Render them with th:text only, never th:utext. Default escaping stays on.

notes: Design-doc writes: docs/system-design.md § Contracts gains rows for SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyRepository, and SpecialtyController (REQ-VET-003), and the Implements column of Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository now includes REQ-VET-003. A new § Scale and Load section, from the doctor template, holds the specialty directory row. No ADR: the in-memory grouping choice belongs to this slice alone, and the row carries it. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records to audit. Vocabulary: 'specialty directory' is a PRD page term but is absent from docs/ubiquitous-language.md. It is flagged for product-requirements-expert and was not written here, because this is not the foundational path. Layout active-menu token: the page belongs to the veterinarian area, so passing 'vets' is acceptable. It adds no entry or link.

findings.description: Both suites substitute SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository, so nothing exercises the real SpecialtyRepository.findAll (derived query on the Specialty entity, documented to include unheld specialties) or real Vet/Specialty instances loaded through the cached VetRepository. grep -F -e SpecialtyRepository over src/test finds only these in-memory stand-ins and the lambda.
